summary:
CONVERGENCE PROTOCOL (controller, binding). Measured churn: F1 has 94 artifact events across 39 paths in 35 minutes, and every new revision draws fresh 'revise' verdicts, so no gate can converge. Effective now:
P1 PUBLISH-AND-FREEZE: publish ONE revision to the canonical paths (schemas/*.yaml, research_map/formulation_taxonomy.yaml), emit artifact events, and declare FINAL FOR RUN. Astra freezes it; no edits for 25 minutes.
P2 BLOCKING TRIAGE: reviewers label each finding B (blocking: class leakage, conclusion inflation, ambiguous quantifier, missing required field, unproved 'equivalently', wrong regularity direction) or N (non-blocking: wording, extra fields, provenance notes, style). Verdict is `revise` ONLY with >=1 B finding; otherwise `accept` with N findings listed as backlog. Repeating a prior round's finding counts as B only if it is still present at the reviewed hash.
P3 ONE MORE REVISION: after this freeze each formulation artifact gets at most ONE revision (N+1). If blocking findings remain after that, the gate stays pending and the item is recorded unresolved for the run. Unresolved is a valid outcome.
P4 HASH BINDING: reviews bind to the published sha256. If the artifact changes mid-review, the review is void and counts against the revision budget.
P5 NO PATH MIGRATION: canonical paths stay schemas/ + research_map/; the authoring tree must mirror at publish.

falsifier: Revision N+1 still edits after the freeze, or blocking findings are marked non-blocking without a reason.

F-2 (major, HF-06): D0 is not well-typed. D0 mixes pair-indexed Sobolev regularities with the smooth-with-decay default, while the binder is (s,delta), G is indexed G_{s,delta}, and X^{s,delta}_vac is pair-indexed; the smooth branch has a Frechet ambient space and no (s,delta) values (line 150). The same leaf also says the class 'is fixed at these values', which conflicts with quantifying over all of D0. Two competent readers can instantiate the class differently (all admissible regularities vs one fixed regime), which is the artifact's own schema_falsifiers[0] at line 282 firing on the domain.

F-3 (major, HF-02-adjacent (binding/metadata, not content leakage)): The class-contract binding does not resolve inside the authoritative artifact. class_contract_pointer line 38 targets artifacts/formulation/formulation_taxonomy.yaml#class_contracts.AF-WCC-VAC-GEN; the controller's canonical artifact research_map/formulation_taxonomy.yaml (276009f4) has no class_contracts key at all (top-level key is classes), and the two copies are not byte-identical (canonical 276009f4 vs authoring c8e979a1). f0_binding.class_contract_supplement line 311 also points at the authoring copy. There are seven duplicate top-level revised_at keys (lines 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 23) and two revised_at_unused keys (lines 26, 28); YAML 1.2 forbids duplicate mapping keys, PyYAML silently keeps the last, and a strict parser errors. That is whole-curve single-q containment, which contradicts the class's own canonical predicate at visibility.definition lines 219-220 (single-q TAIL: exists q AND t0 with gamma([t0,T)) contained in J^-(q)) and contradicts quantifiers.negation line 88, which negates the tail predicate. The expansion is strictly weaker: the schema's own example at line 220 (geodesic that starts in the exterior and ends inside the black-hole region) has a visible tail while the whole curve is not contained in any J^-(q), so it satisfies lines 54-55 but violates the canonical conclusion at line 251. quantifiers.formal and quantifiers.negation are therefore not exact negations of each other, and the class as formally expanded is not equivalent to the F0 AF-WCC-VAC-GEN conclusion object. The canonical gate returns PASS with failed_rules=[] at this hash because R03/R10 check domain resolution and field presence, never agreement with visibility.definition.

HF-06 (major; nearest code, dangling-symbol): conclusion.statement_formal line 251 uses AF_{I+}(M_D), which no leaf of the document defines (grep AF_{I+} matches line 251 only; i_plus.definition line 200 names the concept in prose, and quantifiers D3 line 74 gives the completion) and complete(I+_D), which is defined prose-only at i_plus.completeness_definition line 202. statement: Citation verification of the AF-SCC-C0-VAC-GEN CONVENTION CAVEAT (schemas/af_scc_c0_vacuum.yaml line 99, canonical sha256 1bb78ce9b3572cdac229ad7623ce96908bf4f08dc62c3c6264d97b17c0355508): its cited pointer arXiv:1901.07996 (Grant-Kunzinger-Saemann-Steinbauer, 'The future is not always open', Lett. Math. Phys. 2019, DOI 10.1007/s11005-019-01213-8) SUPPORTS the caveat's factual core at full-text level: chronological futures for continuous (alpha-Holder, 0<alpha<1) metrics may be non-open (Example 3.1, source line 720) and may differ between the smooth/piecewise-C^1 and locally-Lipschitz/absolutely-continuous curve classes (abstract; source lines 190-191; Lemma 2.2, source lines 340-352). The schema's remedy sentence -- 'if the causal relation is degenerate, the witness must instead be a timelike curve from iota(M) to a point of int(M' minus iota(M))' -- is NOT supported by the source: the only openness guarantee the source proves is for the locally-uniformly-timelike / piecewise-C^1 class (Lemma 2.2), and source line 819 shows the pathologies persist even when C^1 curves with finitely many null-tangent points are admitted, so an unqualified 'timelike curve' witness is not class-determined for a merely continuous metric. Verdict PARTIAL; the schema should either pin clause (f)'s degenerate-case witness to the l.u.t./piecewise-C^1 class with a named degeneracy criterion or mark clause (f) an explicit open proof obligation. This claim does NOT assert that the C0 class is open/closed as a theorem, does not resolve clause (f), and does not mark the citation VERIFIED.

statement: On the N0 flat-space spherical scalar-wave calibration (class sub-case AF-WCC-SCALAR-SPH; fixed Minkowski, test field, no self-gravity), an independently implemented direct-variable scheme (implicit Crank-Nicolson on phi with L phi = phi_rr + (2/r) phi_r, regular-centre rule L phi(0)=6(phi_1-phi_0)/dr^2, phi(R)=0, dt=0.5 dr) reproduces the published reduced-scheme results: psi-L2 fit order 1.991437 (r0=10,sigma=1.5) and 1.985789 (r0=2,sigma=1.0, origin-excited, u(0,0)~0.54) vs published cnfd 1.993478, both inside the harness p_tol=0.3; direct and reduced psi fields agree to 3.9e-13 relative; the interior is bitwise identical (0.0 absolute difference) under four different origin rules (6/dr^2, 2/dr^2, garbage coefficients, and phi(0) pinned to 17) whose phi(0) values differ by >=16.9. The reason is algebraic: on this uniform node-centred grid r_i*(L_sph u)_i = (Delta_1D (r u))_i to 2.4e-16 relative and the first interior row's lower coefficient is exactly zero, so the psi=r*phi reduction and the origin treatment are not independent discretisation axes. Taylor-start vs exact-start orders differ by <=0.0025; the spatial order isolated from temporal error (cfl->0 intercepts at fixed dr) is 1.99974/1.99988 with linear-in-dt^2 fits R^2>=0.9999998. Published wiring check: the re-implemented cnfd reproduces the published fit order and row errors to 2.5e-15 relative. Scope limits: fixed Minkowski test field only; the structural identity is specific to this node-centred grid/operator form; artifacts are validation_status=unverified pending reviewer verdict.

findings: F-01 HARD (P3; HF-06 class, independently reproduced at the pinned hash): the exact quantifier prefix and the conclusion block expand DIFFERENT visibility predicates. quantifiers.formal (schemas/af_wcc_vacuum.yaml:54-55) closes with 'not exists q in I+ with gamma subset J^-(q) intersect M' and quantifiers.domains.D5 (:79-81) defines q by 'gamma([0,T)) is contained in the causal past J^-(q)' - both are WHOLE-CURVE single-q containment. The class's one canonical predicate, visibility.definition (:219-220), is the single-q TAIL predicate ('exists q in I+ AND t0 in [0,T) such that the TAIL gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q)'), and conclusion.statement_formal (:251) binds that predicate by name. Direction: whole-curve non-containment A is IMPLIED by tail non-containment B (a tail is a subset of the curve), so A is strictly weaker than the conclusion's negation; a development with a visible tail but no visible whole curve satisfies the formal expansion and violates the conclusion. The schema itself states the whole-curve reading 'would misclassify a geodesic that starts in the exterior and ends inside the black-hole region' (:220) and that single-q non-containment must not be replaced by B-containment (:227); class_identity_variants (:231-244) declares exactly ONE canonical predicate. quantifiers.negation (:85-88) negates the TAIL predicate, so quantifiers.formal and quantifiers.negation are not exact negations of each other. hard_failures.finding: Operative quantifier expansion contradicts the canonical visibility predicate (whole curve vs tail). quantifiers.formal (lines 47-55, decisive clause at 54-55: 'not exists q in I+ with gamma subset J^-(q) intersect M') and domain D5 (lines 79-81: q such that 'gamma([0,T)) is contained in ... J^-(q)') use whole-curve single-q non-containment, and quantifiers.ordered (56-62) binds no t0. visibility.definition (line 220) defines visibility with the tail ('exists q in I+ AND t0 in [0,T) such that the TAIL gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q)') and visibility.negation_conclusion (line 222) is the matching tail negation ('for every q in I+ and every t0 in [0,T), the tail ... is NOT contained'). Since whole-curve containment A(q) implies tail containment B(q,t0) and not conversely, 'not exists q A(q)' is STRICTLY WEAKER than 'not exists q exists t0 B(q,t0)'. quantifiers.negation (84-88) negates the tail predicate ('some ... geodesic ... is visible from I+'), so the formal block and its declared negation are not complements of each other. The R1-F02 tail correction was propagated to the visibility block (R1 tags at 220/222, note at 227) but not into quantifiers.formal/ordered/D5; the earlier whole-curve reading survives in the operative statement and in statement_formal (line 251) only as the undefined symbol AF_{I+}. The class is therefore stated weaker than its own definition, which the artifact's forbidden_weakenings (262-266, 'using a weaker visibility notion or a different definition of singular point') prohibits.

statement: At published module numerics/tests/flat_wave_replication.py#8ade1cdc163e and protocol numerics/CONVERGENCE_PROTOCOL.md#1e6cdf04d7a2, the three schemes published as methodologically independent (lffd, cnfd, cnfem) contain 2 distinct spatial discretisations and 2 distinct time integrators: the lffd and cnfd spatial operators are the same 3-point FD matrix (cnfd.self.A equals the FD matrix with max abs entry diff 0.0; random-state one-step identities pin lffd d2=A*psi to 3.70e-16 and cnfd d2=A*(psi_new+psi_old)/2 to 7.85e-16 relative), and cnfd/cnfem share the Crank-Nicolson integrator, so the published three occupy 3 of the 4 cells of a 2 (spatial: 3-point FD, P1 consistent-mass FEM) x 2 (time: leapfrog, Crank-Nicolson) design. The missing cell (FEM+leapfrog) was implemented in artifacts/worker-051/n0_scheme_axes/ and measures mixed 4-rung order 2.001045 and dt->0 isolated spatial order 1.999993; the published 4-rung orders (lffd 1.9966248643, cnfd 1.9953510344, cnfem 1.9888598802) reproduce bitwise (abs delta 0.0). FEM and FD are distinct operators, not merely differently scaled ones: central-row Nyquist implied eigenvalues are in the exact ratio 3.000000000000000 (dev <= 1.9e-16; 4/h^2 vs 12/h^2), the smooth-mode relative difference decays at fitted order 2.0000 (7.31e-5 at dr=0.2 to 1.14e-6 at dr=0.025), boundary-row relative difference is 0.8231, and the full-matrix Frobenius difference stays O(1) (boundary/grid-scale dominated, explicitly not a convergence metric). Therefore 'independence holds along spatial discretisation' holds at multiplicity 2, not 3, while the order-2 result is corroborated by a complete 2x2 design: all four cells are monotone and within |p-2|<=0.3 in both mixed and dt->0 isolated spatial order. conclusion_type numerical_evidence; flat-space calibration sub-case only.

The threshold s > 5/2 is stated for asymptotically flat vacuum data in Klainerman-Rodnianski arXiv:math/0109173 Theorem 1.1 and Remark 1.2 (attributing the classical result to [H-K-M]), and the decay family is stated in Lindblad-Rodnianski arXiv:math/0312479 (= CMP 256:43-110, 2005) Section 1 as g_0ij = (1+2M/r)delta_ij + o(r^{-1-sigma}), k_0 = o(r^{-2-sigma}), sigma > 0. The exact weighted normalization and the delta in (1/2,1) interval were not found in any of the four checked sources; the checked sources that do treat weighted asymptotically flat phases use a different index-sign convention (Bartnik-Isenberg arXiv:gr-qc/0405092 Section 3: (g-ring + H^2_{-1/2}) x H^1_{-3/2}). Therefore the schema status must remain UNVERIFIED, with the KR2001/LR2005 locators admissible only as partial-support annotations. No theorem, no gate verdict, no schema edit.
